item.text: {"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"During 2023, López Obrador’s record showed both corrective efforts and serious failures to ensure correction, compliance, and remedy. The government created investigative bodies, appointed a special prosecutor, invited independent experts, ordered cooperation, and continued agreements concerning access, arrest warrants, and investigation of obstruction and torture in Ayotzinapa; the CNDH also recorded evidence of full or partial compliance with recommendations and reparative actions by authorities (BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0021-R01-E009). The government also pursued a recovery lawsuit against a former official from the preceding administration, although the allegations and recovery remained unresolved and the conduct was not attributable to López Obrador’s own administration (BATCH-0012-E011). However, the GIEI and other monitors reported that military and intelligence institutions withheld or denied records despite presidential orders, gave changing or contradicted accounts, and that the GIEI ultimately ended its work after continued obstruction. López Obrador defended the military and publicly criticized investigators or organizations supporting victims; these reports support inadequate presidential enforcement and response, but do not establish that he personally ordered the concealment or that every institutional failure was his direction (BATCH-0003-E015; BATCH-0003-E016; BATCH-0008-E002; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0013-E002; BATCH-0013-E003; BATCH-0026-E012). The 2023 reporting on disappearance-count methodology and the 2019–2022 Segalmex matter is relevant as longitudinal context for correction and accountability, but does not by itself establish a discrete 2023 presidential correction failure; the Segalmex record shows acknowledgment and an investigation, alongside the reassignment of the former director rather than a demonstrated complete remedy (BATCH-0013-E011; BATCH-0046-E008; BATCH-0006-E007). Overall, the supplied evidence supports partial and inconsistent correction and remedy, with stronger attribution to López Obrador’s public commitments, orders, and defense of the military than to agency-level concealment or personal intent.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0012-E011","BATCH-0046-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0013-E011","BATCH-0006-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The record does not establish a final presidential correction, complete remedy, recovered harm, or personal intent behind the reported military and intelligence obstruction.","Several favorable items document institutional or governmental action without proving López Obrador’s personal role, while several adverse items concern inherited 2014 conduct or agency noncompliance during the investigation.","The supplied evidence includes advocacy, investigative, and secondary assessments, and does not provide final adjudication for every alleged falsehood, concealment, or accountability failure."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported compression that López Obrador generally denied or attacked investigators instead of correcting the record; the revised answer distinguishes presidential rhetoric from agency obstruction and avoids treating all responses as reactions to conclusively established presidential error.","Added the omitted contrary evidence on GIEI agreements, CNDH compliance and reparative actions, UN coordination context, and the García Luna recovery lawsuit, while limiting what those items establish.","Separated direct 2023 evidence from longitudinal or inherited context, especially the 2019–2022 Segalmex matter and the 2014 Ayotzinapa events.","Qualified attribution, intent, and remedy claims where the supplied passages do not establish personal presidential direction or final outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A final judgment would benefit from primary records documenting López Obrador’s specific orders, responses after notice, disciplinary decisions, public corrections, and any completed remedies during 2023.","The ledger should separately track the status and outcome of the Ayotzinapa document requests, GIEI mandate, arrest warrants, victim reparations, disappearance-count methodology, and Segalmex investigations.","Further review is warranted if evidence emerges directly linking presidential knowledge, benefit, authorization, or retaliation to the reported obstruction or alleged falsehoods."]}
